messages:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED ALERT: ELB healthcheck fail rate > 35% across us-west-2b targets for service 'api-redwood'. Trigger: 5xx surge, sustained 3m. Suggested paging: oncall.
alice (oncall): acked. I'm pulling LB/ASG/EC2 + EBS metrics now. Can someone grab Route53 health checks? @mike @maya
alice (oncall): quick summary from cloudwatch: ELB 5xx -> spike at 02:07 UTC, target unhealthy count rising. Instance CPU normal, but EBSReadOps latency spiking on 3 instances in us-west-2b.
mike (sre): saw it. Jumping on host logs. Suspect EBS IO contention -> app thread timeouts -> healthcheck failures. Starting ssh/diag.
mike (sre): log snippet: ```
2026-03-15T02:06:38Z ERROR http-handler: upstream request timeout (read timeout)
2026-03-15T02:06:39Z WARN disk: read I/O latency 1200ms device /dev/nvme1n1
``` 
maya (eng-network): also seeing intermittent cross-AZ packet drops between us-west-2b <-> us-west-2a per VPC flow logs. Pattern aligns with instance failures but looks like a networking flap was ongoing at same time window.
alice (oncall): classification P1. Customer impact: 8-11% of traffic failing (region-weighted). Escalating to full incident. #inc-standup
pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall rotation: alice (oncall). Notifying primary escalation: mike (sre).
alice (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) stop sending traffic to us-west-2b via Route53 weight shift; 2) drain ELB targets in 2b; 3) replace suffering instances (ASG replace); 4) investigate EBS metrics and check for noisy neighbor/IOPS limits.
alice (oncall): @tom can you prepare a Route53 weight change (move 25% -> other region) and update status page? jess, can you queue customer notifications for affected tenants (approx 120 customers)?
tom (prodops): will do. Preparing runbook step to shift weighted routing: set us-west-2 weight 0.25 -> 0. Split remainder to us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Executing in 60s.
jess (support): drafting status: "We are investigating increased error rates for API traffic in our US-west region. Mitigation in progress." Will post after tom confirms weight change.
alice (oncall): executing ELB drain command now to avoid new sessions to unhealthy targets. ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-0abc123 --region us-west-2``` Doing in batches of 2.
mike (sre): ASG replace triggered: ```aws autoscaling terminate-instances-in-auto-scaling-group --instance-ids i-0abc123 --should-decrement-desired-capacity false``` Replacing three instances that show EBS high-latency. Monitoring recovery.
mike (sre): Observing fast retry errors in app: database calls timing out due to node-level stuck I/O. EBS metrics: BurstBalance exhausted on gp3 volumes for those instances.
maya (eng-network): added fw logs: a couple of ENIs reported RX drops ~200pps for ~4m window. I've opened a ticket with AWS NOC (case 1234567890) with flow logs attached.
alice (oncall): tom, please proceed with Route53 weight change when ready. We'll hold 0.25 shift to avoid capacity pressure on other regions.
tom (prodops): applied weight change: Route53 record "api.redwood" now: us-west-2: 25%, us-east-1: 50%, eu-west-1: 25%. TTL lowered to 30s. Confirming propagation.
alice (oncall): update: within 90s we see 5xx rate drop in global agg, and latency for remaining us-west targets improving. Customer impact trending down from 10% -> 3%.
jess (support): posted status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-15-usw2-elb . Customers DMing support asking about retries; sending recommended client-side retry guidance.
mike (sre): replacing EBS volumes on replaced instances with larger gp3 IOPS baseline to avoid burst exhaustion. Doing snapshot and recreate for immutable infra pattern.
mike (sre): mitigation verification: new instances healthy, application latency normalizing. EBS latency back to baseline on replacements.
maya (eng-network): AWS NOC responded: isolated networking fabric issue affecting subset of AZ us-west-2b; they applied a hardware-level remediation and reported partial restoration ~02:30 UTC. We still see residual ENI resets; keeping watch.
alice (oncall): brief timeline so far: 02:06 alert -> 02:09 drain/start replace -> 02:12 Route53 weights -> 02:18 5xx drop -> 02:30 AWS NOC note. Good. Next steps: hold weights for 30m, monitor, then gradual traffic shift back only when stable for 15m.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff reminder: alice (oncall) will remain for next 30m, if stability holds escalate back to normal ops.
mike (sre): postmortem notes to capture: correlated EBS BurstBalance exhaustion + AZ-level network packet drops amplified failure domain. Need to add runbook clause: if EBS gp3 BurstBalance low + ENI drops, prefer R/I placement & proactive route53 shift.
jess (support): collecting list of affected customers and preparing targeted emails. Estimated impacted: customers with high session stickiness routed to us-west-2b — approximately 120 tenants, highest impact for 10 enterprise accounts, outreach in progress.
alice (oncall): deciding severity label SEV2-> SEV1 briefly due to customer-facing errors; downgraded to SEV2 as majority traffic diverted and error rate below thresholds.
mike (sre): will follow up with infra to evaluate gp3 baseline IOPS for critical ASGs, consider moving to provisioned IOPS for hot paths.
maya (eng-network): will sync with AWS account team tomorrow for deeper network correlation. Also will check whether any ENI placement changes needed for redundancy.
alice (oncall): closing: continuing monitoring. If 5xx remains <1% for 20m and no new ENI resets, we'll begin gradual traffic return. Thanks team, great quick coordination :thumbsup:
tom (prodops): documenting DNS weight change + rollback steps in incident ticket.
jess (support): final note: posted customer update at 02:40 UTC and will send targeted emails to high-touch customers.
mike (sre): leaving logs & commands used in the incident ticket.
alice (oncall): handing off to next oncall in 30m; next oncall: mike (sre). If anything spikes, @mike please take lead. Closing active paging but keeping channel open for followups.
